mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative more than 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive more than 50% of the time when UNRATE exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but 60-day returns are negative more than 30% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts and retail sales together signal strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies rise but returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests increased economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases by 5% but 60-day returns are negative more than 35% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation as measured by CPI allows for accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI is low but 20-day returns are negative more than 45% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth above 2% annually indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth exceeds 2% but 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment combined with low payroll employment suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies indicate weakness but 60-day returns are positive more than 35% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.
